items.basis: IMF programme approved in 2025 after years of high inflation.
why: Shows how years of high inflation erode wages and savings.
Argentina is the IMF's largest borrower, so its programme shapes policy at home.
Its recovery is watched across Latin America.

items.basis: IMF Extended Fund Facility since 2024; tight public finances.
why: Repeated IMF programmes show a cycle of borrowing and reform.
Debt payments leave less money for schools and hospitals.
Stability matters in a nuclear-armed country of about 240 million people.

items.basis: IMF programme and pressure on the currency.
why: Egypt buys much of its food and fuel abroad, so a weak currency raises prices.
Suez Canal income fell when Red Sea shipping was disrupted.
Gulf states and the IMF have stepped in with large support.
The World Bank ranks it among the worst economic crises since the mid-1800s.
Many people lost access to their bank savings.
